messages:
Customer - ACME Integrations: Hey team, since the cert rotation at ~02:10 UTC we're seeing a lot of 502/504s from your hosted inference endpoint (api.redwood-hosted.example.com). Spike started ~02:12 and has been intermittent. We can reproduce with a simple curl: 
Customer - ACME Integrations: `curl -v https://api.redwood-hosted.example.com/v1/generate -H "Authorization: Bearer <key>"` -> TLS handshake timeout or 502 gateway sometimes. This is impacting our customers, can you help? :frowning: 

Maria G: sorry you're hit, thanks for flagging. I'm looking now. Can you paste the exact request id/response body from one of the 502s if you have it? Any headers we should be aware of? Also which region are you hitting (us-east-1/us-west-2/eu)? 

Customer - ACME Integrations: we see it from us-east-1 (client-hosted in VA). Example response: `HTTP/1.1 502 Bad Gateway
content-type: application/json
{x-request-id: 0a3b2c...}` and body `{"error":"upstream connect error: TLS handshake timeout"}`. Request id: `0a3b2c9f`. Happened on multiple pods. 

Jamie (oncall): @Maria grabbing traces. I can see retries and TLS timeouts for request id 0a3b2c9f on our edge logs. Suspect DNS/edge cert combo during rotation. I'm running a quick `dig` and `curl` from our edge tooling toward the customer's gateway: 
```
; dig +short api.redwood-hosted.example.com @8.8.8.8
bindings: 
nyc-edge-1.redwood-edge.net.
nyc-internal-01.internal.redwood-edge.net.  ;; <-- intermittent CNAME returned here too

# curl -v --connect-timeout 5 https://api.redwood-hosted.example.com/v1/health
* TCP connection to api.redwood-hosted.example.com:443 failed: Operation timed out
* Closing connection 0
```
Looks like our resolver sometimes returns an internal CNAME that doesn't have the public cert chain yet (hence handshake timeout/mismatch). Possibly a propagation/TTL issue during cert rollout. 

Leo N: adding context — we rotated certificates in the edge fleet at 02:08 UTC. There was a staged rollout across regions; TTLs for the CNAMEs were 300s but some resolvers still had stale entries. There's a race where the new cert is present on new hostnames but older resolvers keep the pre-rotation CNAME that points to a node without the new chain. That produces handshake failures or timeouts while the node is being reprovisioned. 

Ravi P: I'm pulling the edge deploy logs now. @Jamie can you grep for that request id in the edge proxy logs? Also check if any of the affected nodes returned a 521/connection reset from the origin. 

Jamie (oncall): Grepped the proxy logs. For 0a3b2c9f I see: `WARN upstream: handshake timeout after 10s -> connection dropped; upstream host: nyc-internal-01.internal.redwood-edge.net` and then `fallback to backup-route -> 502 returned`. We also had a flurry of resolver SERVFAILs reported by our resolver mesh around 02:11-02:14. 

Maria G: OK this looks like a cert rotation + DNS propagation flap. Immediate mitigations: 
- Rolling back the cert rollout to previous chain for the small subset of edge hosts returning internal CNAME (we've kicked that now). 
- Forcing a short TTL change and purging our internal resolver caches for the impacted pop (nyc). 
- Enabling temporary 10s extended connect-timeout to reduce 502/early failures while node reprovisions. 

Customer - ACME Integrations: thanks, appreciate the quick actions. Any ETA on full resolution? We're still seeing intermittent errors on some clients (mobile) that might be hitting different resolvers. 

Leo N: We're forcing a global cache flush but note that some public resolvers (ISP caches) won't respect pushes. We're also going to add a pre-warm step to future rollouts to publish the new cert to the CNAME targets before changing DNS. ETA for visible reduction: 10-20 mins; full convergence 45-60 mins depending on ISP TTLs. 

Ravi P: follow-up checks: ran `openssl s_client -connect nyc-edge-1.redwood-edge.net:443 -servername api.redwood-hosted.example.com -showcerts` against the host that returned the bad CNAME, got timeout first but then success after purge — the cert chain served matched the previous chain (rolled back). 
```
CONNECTED(00000003)
depth=2 C = US, O = Redwood Inference, CN = Redwood Root CA
subject=CN = api.redwood-hosted.example.com
---
SSL handshake has read 3276 bytes and written 456 bytes
---
```

sre-bot: alert cleared for `edge-tls-handshake-surge-nyc` (was firing 02:12-02:17 UTC) :white_check_mark: 

Maria G: I also requested billing queue to apply a small credit for the 20-30 minute window for affected API calls for ACME. We'll follow up on comms once we confirm all resolvers have converged. 

Customer - ACME Integrations: confirmed lower error rate from our side. Mobile clients still showing occasional timeout (ISP cache maybe) but much better. Appreciate the credit and the detailed postmortem when available. 

Maria G: closing loop for now — root cause = simultaneous cert rollout + DNS CNAME propagation race -> some resolvers received a CNAME to nodes without the new cert chain -> upstream TLS handshake timeouts and 502s. Action items: 
- engineering to add pre-warm publish step to cert rollout playbook (Leo)
- lower DNS TTL before rotate and schedule staggered rollout windows (Ravi)
- improve resolver health checks to detect SERVFAIL spikes and auto-rollback (Jamie)
- support to confirm credits and send formal incident summary (Maria)

Customer - ACME Integrations: sounds good. Please ping when the postmortem is ready. Thanks all. :pray:
